highlights.title: Websites taken down worldwide as critical cyber-security update issued
highlights.summary: The vulnerabilities with PHP, a programming language widely used across the internet, have been described as the most significant ever found by AI.
body: International governments and agencies have urged websites to address two critical cyber-security flaws in a programming language which powers much of the internet.
The vulnerabilities were found within the PHP programming language, with a fix issued on Wednesday afternoon.

Multiple cyber-security agencies have urged organisations unable to apply fixes in time to consider taking their sites down, leaving bodies such as the Finnish government, Edinburgh council and the BBC to take pages offline.
The flaws were discovered by AI, with cyber-security firm Wiz saying they were the "most severe vulnerabilities ever discovered" by the tech, which is reshaping the cyber landscape.

highlights.title: Conversational Gemini navigation comes to Apple CarPlay
highlights.summary: After introducing its Gemini AI assistant to Android Auto last year, Google is now bringing it to Apple CarPlay users. The conversational Gemini in navigation is available today for US drivers, with "rollout happening globally too," according to Google (we've asked for specific regional…
body: CarPlay users in the US can now use Gemini to chat with Google Maps.

It’s taken almost 12 months for Google to bring this to CarPlay users, but now they can talk to the voice assistant in Google Maps to get some hands-free help while driving. That includes asking it multi-step questions, such as recommendations on places to visit and then prompting it to direct you there while avoiding toll roads. Users can activate the feature by tapping the Gemini icon in Google Maps on their Car’s infotainment display.

Google describes this CarPlay support update as a conversational way to report traffic disruptions and find information about stops and places on-the-go. There’s no mention of any of the Personal Intelligence features that were announced yesterday for Gemini in Android Auto and cars with Google built-in, however, which enable the voice assistant to access user information from Google apps, including Gmail, Calendar, Maps, Photos, YouTube, and Search. We’ve asked Google if CarPlay users will also receive the personalization update and will update if we hear back.

highlights.title: England 'not thinking about points difference' against France
highlights.summary: England hooker Brad O'Neill says his side will resist the urge to go for broke when they face France in their second Rugby League World Cup match in Perth on Saturday.
body: An opening 30-12 defeat to Tonga has left their hopes of reaching the semi-finals hanging by a thread, with points difference looking increasingly like the only way to progress.
But head coach Brian McDermott has named an unchanged 19-man matchday squad, a sign that he does not plan radical changes against a France team smarting from their 78-4 humbling by Samoa.
O'Neill, the newly-crowned Super League Man of Steel, said: "We have discussed what is required but I feel like the mentality can't be any different to what we had against Tonga.

"We can't go into this game thinking about the points difference. We've got to go into this game hard-nosed like we did against Tonga, and hopefully if we do our jobs well enough we're going to get the win."

highlights.title: How to play DMZ solo in Modern Warfare 4
highlights.summary: A lot of people are wondering how to play DMZ solo in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, or even whether it's actually possible in the first place. I bring good news: it is definitely possible, but the setting is a little hidden, and chances are, you'll load into your first game without even seeing…
body: Here's an explainer on how to play solo in DMZ in Modern Warfare 4, and the benefits of doing so.

When you're getting ready to deploy from your forward-operating base, select your deployment choice (story mission, dynamic operation, or free roam), then choose your infil method. Then you'll be shown a screen with your operator, your inventory, whether you want to equip a free loadout or not, and more.

In the very bottom left of this screen, there's a small toggle that says "squad fill." If you want to play solo, make sure this is turned off. Doing so will ensure you load into DMZ by yourself, rather than having random teammates with you.

If you're traditionally a solo player, this is obviously great news, but playing solo has a few different benefits in DMZ. Firstly, you get to keep all the loot you find to yourself. It also means it's easier to stay stealthy and avoid enemies, whether they're real players or PvE soldiers. Finally, it also means you can do whichever story missions and dynamic operations you like, rather than having to go for what someone else wants.

highlights.title: MNEK cancels tour over lack of ticket sales and high production costs
highlights.summary: The Grammy-nominated artist was due to start a run of shows for his latest album Bulldozer!! next month.
body: MNEK has cancelled his upcoming tour due to a lack of ticket sales and the show not being "ready to the standard" he wanted.
In a statement shared on Instagram, the 31-year-old said he joins other artists who have cancelled shows recently as a result of "high production costs" and "over-ambitious planning".
Earlier this year, The Pussycat Dolls called off almost the entire US leg of their reunion tour following poor ticket sales.
The singer, whose real name is Uzoechi Emenike, said he had been "really looking forward" to performing his new album but had "no interest in doing this tour if I can't do it right".

highlights.title: Jess Cartner-Morley on fashion: don’t want to get your Big Winter Coat out just yet? Try ‘onion dressing’
highlights.summary: It’s time to learn the art of layering – and we’re talking a crew neck with a ballet wrap and blazer, not full-on outdoor explorer. Is layering an art? Probably not in the traditional sense. We are not talking the Bayeux tapestry here.
body: The avant-garde layering term to drop in order to sound like a connoisseur this season is onion dressing. Not the most romantic name, but a clear visual for the most refined form of layering, which is fine layers rather than hefty ones. And instead of the top layer covering all beneath it, each piece should be visible. As if we were slicing through the onion and looking at a cross-section if you will excuse me labouring the allium thing. This is layering with finesse rather than brute force. Hems and collars and cuffs give an outfit depth and texture without adding too much bulk. You want to look intriguing and multi-dimensional, not like Joey in Friends wearing all of Chandler’s clothes.

highlights.title: Supernatural’s comeback starts today, with more music and VR workouts coming soon
highlights.summary: Despite Meta saying it would stop creating new content for Supernatural, the beloved fitness VR game is back after spinning off to go its own way and is relaunching with an Early Access preview in the Meta Horizon Store.
body: Supernatural is relaunching in early access, but it comes with a higher subscription price.

Starting next week, Supernatural will get new workouts every week. The game’s developers also write, “More back-catalog favorites will return in the weeks and months ahead, with new music, higher-definition destinations and new features on the way.”

Other new features coming later include the return of Supernatural Together, which has been “rebuilt from the ground up.” Supernatural is also getting a mobile companion app it says members can use to “Track progress and heart rate and stay connected beyond the headset.”

Supernatural says people who played the original version of the game “can transfer their points, start date, streaks, favorites and badges” to the new version through December 3rd. It’s also offering rewards for “founding members,” starting with a custom bat, with more coming throughout early access.

highlights.title: AI Guardrails Aren’t Stopping Criminal Hackers
highlights.summary: Hackers around the world are all-in on using agentic AI to wage attacks—and manipulating tools like Anthropic’s Claude to help them carry out their crimes.
body: As AI adoption spreads among both malicious hackers and defenders, even relatively unsophisticated cybercriminals are incorporating agentic AI into their campaigns and getting around model safeguards, according to new details published on Wednesday about recent successful attacks by four different threat groups.

“You can leverage different models for different aspects in the operation. Model routing and selection is very important because it’s expensive and a lot of times would be overkill to use newer models,” says Adam Meyers, CrowdStrike's senior vice president of counter adversary work. The researchers observed the attackers using both open- and closed-weight models; in almost all cases, they were using older versions rather than working with frontier models. Meyers notes that doing as much as possible with older models is common in legitimate AI usage, too, as costs mount.
The attackers also used multiple models to take advantage of differences in the guardrails meant to prevent people from using AI to carry out digital attacks.

highlights.title: England star Kildunne dropped for Canada rematch
highlights.summary: Ellie Kildunne has been dropped to the bench in the England Red Roses squad to face Canada on Friday, a week on from suffering defeat in Toronto which ended a 41-match unbeaten run.
body: Head coach John Mitchell has made four changes to the starting XV in total, with Gloucester-Hartpury duo Emma Sing and Mia Venner coming into the back three at full-back and wing respectively, while Helena Rowland of Loughborough Lightning returns at inside-centre.
In the forwards, there is just one amendment to the team that began the second Test - Sadia Kabeya, also of Loughborough Lightning, is selected at openside flanker.
While Kildunne - 2024's World Player of the Year - and back-row Alex Matthews move to the replacements bench, wing Claudia Moloney-MacDonald and centre Tatyana Heard drop out of the squad altogether.

"Last Friday, we lost sight of what we could control when it mattered most; that's on us to fix. This week is about getting back to who we are: hungry, accountable to each other and demanding more of ourselves than anyone outside this group ever could.

body: The update arrives 22nd October on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series S/X, with the Switch 2 version following "in a couple of days", CDPR media manager Laura Beitzel said during a RedStream this afternoon.

Actual details on the new Edgerunners-related story quest were intentionally thin, but Cyberpunk 2 associate game director Pawel Sasko said it had been written with people involved in the Netflix show, and CDPR publishing producer Natlia Pych it would be a prequel to Edgerunners 2. "It will be the last job of the King's team," Pych said, and it will let us meet characters on the team: Emily, Meshuga, and Miguel.
There'll also be a new Edgerunners radio station added to Cyberpunk 2077 to listen to, which has 16 tracks comprised of songs from both Edgerunners 1 and 2, Sasko said.

highlights.title: Supercell completes full acquisition of Metacore
highlights.summary: Supercell has completed its acquisition of Metacore, taking 100% ownership of the Merge Mansion maker. The deal has brought Metacore’s games team into the fold, having "officially started their journey as Supercellians" supported by Supercell peers.
body: Supercell and Metacore originally announced the planned acquisition this May, when Supercell’s intentions to acquire the remainder of the Finnish studio and its flagship game went public. Supercell was already Metacore’s largest shareholder.
Alongside the purchase, Metacore announced it would be cutting up to 160 roles in Finland as part of a restructuring effort.

Months later, Supercell revealed the deal had been signed and that plans for Metacore’s integration were underway. It was expected that the deal would close at the end of September, but it has ultimately taken until today, October 19th, for an official announcement.

"We can finally share that the Supercell acquisition of Metacore and Merge Mansion has been closed. Merge Mansion will transition to be part of Supercell’s game portfolio, and Metacore is now 100% owned by Supercell," Metacore posted on LinkedIn.

highlights.title: I’ve booked my first proper holiday – and it’s pulled me out of winter grimness like a magic spell
highlights.summary: Anticipating a potential spring in which I am bathed in sun on a Greek island is giving me the kind of glee that makes anything feel possible. Reader, it’s important to tell you that I’ve never been to Greece in my life. Not once. But I might be going, for the very first time, in the spring.
body: More than the treat of a fortnight somewhere far away and yet in the company of old, dear friends, what I’m feeling most acutely is the pleasure of a promise. Having something to look forward to? A balm in the best of times. But especially so right now. I am re-emerging from beneath the cloud of the fourth (and fifth!) trimester. I read – and finished – a book the other week. I worked out with a kettlebell at some point in the past month. I went to a gig! Things are feeling viable again.

Outside of my little sphere, having something pleasurable on the horizon feels like a magic spell. There is a grimness to reading headlines in the morning that can’t be shaken off. Going on holiday clearly won’t solve these problems but my Cretan dreams give my soul small moments of uncomplicated anticipatory glee that make life worth living despite the horrors of near and far. Spring will come again, as it always does. The human race trudges on.

Perhaps I feel my most human when I am anticipating. Inside of that anticipation is the incredible knowledge that while everything is possible, sometimes I get to imagine only delightful things. It’s an excellent exercise. Like I said, a magic spell.

highlights.title: The $15 billion ad-powered AI startup your doctor may already be using
highlights.summary: Nearly two-thirds of US doctors are turning to an AI-powered search engine to make patient decisions, propelling a little-known tech startup to a $15 billion valuation while prompting a debate over the future of patient care.
body: Miami-based OpenEvidence, founded by serial entrepreneur Daniel Nadler in 2022, said that many of America’s 1 million physicians processed more than 42 million prompts last month. Doctors are using the company’s chatbot to scour medical journals and clinical guidelines to help diagnose and treat patients.

The ads-powered platform has grown largely by word of mouth, penetrating a sector where few tools have seen similar traction. “We’re the first viral consumer internet app in healthcare,” Nadler told the FT in an interview.
OpenEvidence has won praise from medical professionals who have found it helped ease workloads, according to interviews with eight senior physicians.

But it faces a nascent threat from large AI companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic, who are making a push into the space. Its growing influence has also prompted scrutiny from researchers concerned over the accuracy of its results, as doctors grow more dependent on an AI tool shaping the course of treatments.

highlights.title: Conan, Doris, Crowley absent from Ireland's Nations Championship squad
highlights.summary: Andy Farrell's Ireland will head into November's Nations Championship without injured trio Jack Conan, Caelan Doris and Jack Crowley, but Jamison Gibson-Park has been included.
body: Ireland face Tests against Argentina, Fiji and South Africa next month without captain Caelan Doris and fly-half Jack Crowley, who are both expected to return from long-term injuries in January.

Doris has been sidelined by foot and knee problems, while Crowley is recovering from a vascular issue in his leg. Conan, who like Doris plays at No 8, is also ruled out after injuring his shoulder while playing for Leinster in the Champions Cup last weekend.

Scrum-half Jamison Gibson-Park has yet to feature this season due to a groin injury but has been included in the 36-man squad. Mack Hansen, Andrew Porter and Ryan Baird also return to the squad after recovering from injury.
Two uncapped players have made the squad in Ulster fly-half Jamie Benson and back-row James McNabney, while Dan Sheehan has been named as captain.

highlights.title: GTA 6 Might Give America A Very Expensive Sick Day
highlights.summary: Everyone wants to play Rockstar Games' upcoming heist-'em-up Grand Theft Auto 6 --so much so that some 1.5 million Americans are projected to call in sick to work on November 19 to play the game, which an economics professor estimates will set the country back roughly $1 billion.
body: According to an International Business Times report, economics professor José García Montalvo projected that the 1.5 million workers planning to play hooky to traipse around Leonida next month could cost America a boatload of money. If each worker has an annual salary of $70,000, Montalvo suggests that the math works out to $1 billion, with GTA 6 publisher Take-Two Interactive estimated to make that same amount on November 19.

That's the catch. The American economy isn't necessarily losing money; the bills are just changing hands, from the pockets of the country writ large to those of one multi-billion-dollar corporation. I'm sure you know the saying: The rich get richer.
It's worth noting, though, that this isn't an official forecast. Rather, Montalvo's estimation is a mere academic projection.

highlights.title: No hands required: I found the six best slip-on shoes after months of testing
highlights.summary: After a back injury, bending to put on shoes was unimaginable. I’ve since been testing pairs easy to glide my feet into – and on the eyes. What do you want to know about kitchen and food safety? Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: I popped a disc in my spine a few months back, and one of the things that saved me a lot of pain during my recovery was slip-on shoes. With these, I could wear shoes that looked normal without the pain of bending over to put them on and do up the laces. I have been testing new pairs since then, looking at the various ways that manufacturers such as Kizik, Skechers and others create a shoe that you can slip on as easily as a pair of slippers, but which still look like normal shoes you could wear to work, socializing or anywhere.

I tested seven different pairs of shoes, rating them for ease of use, style, comfort and the intangibles that make you feel comfortable and more confident, no matter how much your back might be aching.

highlights.title: A Design Flaw in Share Links Exposes Users’ Personal Conversations With Meta’s Muse
highlights.summary: The company is suspending the feature after security researchers discovered how easy it was to access sensitive information shared with the AI assistant.
body: Muse, the new general-purpose AI agent from Meta, can expose sensitive information when users share conversations through web links, researchers reported Monday. In response to questions from Ars about the behavior, Meta said it’s suspending the sharing feature while the company reviews it and considers making changes.

Like many online services, Muse has allowed users to share searches, conversations, images, and similar content with other people. Such share features usually involve clicking an option to create a unique URL that anyone can use to load a page hosting the content. To keep potentially sensitive information from being accessible to unintended people, the URLs typically contain a long sequence of text that can’t be easily guessed.
“If you had asked us beforehand, we would have guessed that gathering these would take real effort,” the researchers wrote. “It took one query.”

highlights.title: ‘I’m always being real’: what on earth persuades disgraced people like Elizabeth Holmes to let the cameras in?
highlights.summary: With You Can See Everything, Holmes joins other such high-profile subjects as Lance Armstrong, Imelda Marcos and Anthony Weiner to allow film-makers to document their lives. But do they ever come out well?
body: That question of authenticity is at the heart of documentary film-making. You Can See Everything is as much about the ambiguous relationship between film-maker and subject as it is about Holmes herself. There is often a power struggle over narrative control in documentaries, with both sides of the dynamic wanting different outcomes from the final film. Watching You Can See Everything inevitably prompts the question: why would Holmes, days before she heads to jail, invite the scrutiny of a film crew?

Some people, like Holmes, think a documentary will help rebuild their reputation after public disgrace. When Anthony Weiner, who resigned from Congress after tweeting a photo of his bulging groin, tried to stage a professional comeback with a New York mayoral bid, he allowed cameras to film the journey. Only, he had more to hide: when further sex scandals emerged, his campaign went from a story of public redemption to innuendo-laden humiliation. And all the while, the cameras kept rolling. Weiner is a prime example of a subject losing control of the narrative.

But Xbox Game Pass continues to chug along, welcoming a wave of new games twice a month while bidding farewell to other titles in the library.
body: Originally released back in 1993 by LucasArts, Day of the Tentacle is a wildly influential point-and-click adventure game known for its use of the SCUMM game engine. It allows players to choose from a set of commands at the bottom of the screen — such as "pick up," "talk to," and "use" — and then interact with an object in the world. Double Fine secured the rights to the game from LucasArts after the enthusiastic response to another collaboration between the two studios, 2015's Grim Fandango Remastered (which also leaves Game Pass at the end of the month).

If you're a point-and-click superfan, Day of the Tentacle Remastered is effectively a two-for-one deal — the remaster also includes a fully playable version of LucasArts' 1987 game Maniac Mansion, another wildly influential adventure game that marked the first-ever use of the SCUMM game engine.

“To be part of this AI economy, you don’t want to just be consuming the AI. You want to be producing the AI,” he told the 4,000-strong crowd at Nvidia’s GTC. “We can do all of that here in Europe.”

Calif identified a critical flaw using GPT‑5.6 Sol as part of our Patch the Planet ⁠ (opens in a new window) initiative, with Wiz also independently discovering and reporting both vulnerabilities. For organizations using PHP, the priority now is applying the fixes. We’re sharing a PHP version checker as a Codex skill ⁠ (opens in a new window) to help operators identify potentially vulnerable PHP versions and, alongside PHP’s and their providers’ guidance, determine which updates apply.

highlights.title: New prize launches for books co-written with AI
highlights.summary: After months of controversy over the possible use of AI by winners of prestigious awards, the Prix Pascal de Littérature IA is rewarding fiction written with the help of LLMs. A prize for AI-written books has launched this week.
body: The Prix Pascal de Littérature IA invites submissions of manuscripts co-written with AI tools, with the winner promised publication.

Entrants are asked to submit an unpublished manuscript of between 10,000 and 50,000 words, along with information about which AI model and prompt were used to generate the text. All major language models are allowed, including ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and LLaMA. Entrants can be based anywhere, but entries must be submitted in French.

The Prix Pascal is named after Blaise Pascal, a French polymath who helped invent one of the first mechanical calculators and also wrote theological texts, including Pensées, which Pope Francis praised for its “philosophical depth and literary charm”.

While the terms and conditions ask for a work of fiction, the prize also states that submitted texts should help solve an ethical, social or ecological problem threatening humanity. The prize was founded by Philippe Rodriguez, Albin Serviant and Gilles Mentré, all of whom are technology entrepreneurs.

highlights.title: Beyond Good & Evil 2 reportedly still in development 18 years after being announced, now a "solo-first" adventure now
highlights.summary: Beyond Good & Evil 2 is reportedly still in pre-production a staggering 18 years after it was first announced, and it has apparently evolved from being a multiplayer-first project to being "solo-first" and story based, with additional, optional co-op.
body: Origami Media (in a French report translated by DeepL) said it heard from several people close to the game's development that the idea for Beyond Good and Evil 2, in 2019-2022, was for the game to be "highly multiplayer and connected", featuring "a multitude of planets" where players would be matchmade and play together. Sound familiar? It's supposed to.

"The key concept was the 'third place' - a spot where you might hang out with mates after work, just as you would in Fortnite or Destiny," Origami shared, "which were cited as sources of inspiration. You played as a blank character, tagging along on the adventures of the heroes of Beyond Good & Evil, in the passenger seat."

But since then, the project "evolved", from smaller matchmade groups to more open-ended play, then to team-based play in groups of four and finally, to pairs. "The aim now is to offer a 'solo-first' adventure, with no mandatory online connection and featuring a strong narrative that can also be played in co-op," Origami stated.
"A few years ago, some people thought it bore a resemblance to Zelda in space; today, its combat is very reminiscent of Insomniac's Spider-Man games."
